quote: The Science Behind Sudoku - Jean-Paul Delahaye, Scientific American, June 2006
note: This is a sub-case of Sudoku. The requirement that puzzles have exactly one solution was formalized as a design principle by Nikoli in 1986. The question 'How many puzzles have exactly one solution?' (as distinct from 'how many valid completed grids exist') was explicitly posed by Delahaye in June 2006 in Scientific American. Prior work (2003-2005) had enumerated completed grids (~6.67 × 10^21), but Delahaye highlighted the much harder problem: how many essentially different puzzles (partial grids with unique solutions) exist.
